clue.text: Much better, so enjoying greater popularity

definitions.meaning: the exclamation of approval when something improves: that's an improvement
read literally, people like the thing more, so it is more liked

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom of approval for an improvement, and read word by word it says something is liked more.

clue.text: An absolute prerequisite for immature wine

definitions.meaning: something you cannot do without, an essential
grape juice before or during fermentation, new wine

explanation.definitionFit: An essential thing is something one has to have; new unfermented grape juice is also called by this word in winemaking.

clue.text: Do what our first parents did-kick up a fuss

definitions.text: Do what our first parents did
definitions.meaning: Adam and Eve brought up their son Cain, the first child in Genesis
make a noisy commotion, cause trouble

explanation.definitionFit: Adam and Eve reared their son Cain, and the idiom for creating an uproar uses the same words.

clue.text: Did he misuse a rifle?

indicators.note: the letters of the weapon's name are put to wrong use, scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: A question about whether some prisoner once handled a gun wrongly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misuse' rearranges RIFLE. The whole clue doubles as the definition: someone jailed for life may well have misused a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner serving a life sentence is often someone convicted of killing, perhaps with a gun.

clue.text: Sauce boat now costs more!

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat
a price that has risen has gone up

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that the gravy boat has gone up in price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce boat' reads as one item of tableware, but the definition stops at 'Sauce' and 'boat' is the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the tomato condiment, a sauce served with chips and burgers.

clue.text: Anyone in the know keeps to the

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Anyone in the know keeps to the (7)', ends mid-phrase after 'the'; the rest is lost in OCR and a search of the exact text finds nothing.
annotationWithheld.clue: Anyone in the know keeps to the

clue.text: Small bird needs one small tree

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A tiny bird needs a single little tree to perch in.
explanation.definitionFit: The titi is a shrub or small tree of the south-eastern United States, sometimes called leatherwood.

clue.text: One nice way Boadicea ruled

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: nice in a way: the word is taken in an altered fashion, its letters reordered

explanation.surface: A remark that the ancient British queen governed in a pleasant manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way' is the anagram signal, as in 'nice in a way'. Boadicea (Boudicca) was queen of the East Anglian tribe that rose against Rome in AD 60.
explanation.definitionFit: Boudicca was queen of this Celtic tribe of East Anglia, so they were the people she governed.

clue.text: Cuts should bury religious differences

parts.note: to inter is to bury a body
sects are breakaway religious groups, divided by doctrine

explanation.surface: A plea that budget cuts should end disputes between faiths.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines that cross one another divide each other, so the verb means crosses or divides.

clue.text: Omit a Jewish festival

definitions.meaning: as two words, a verb phrase meaning skip or leave out
the spring feast commemorating the Exodus from Egypt

explanation.definitionFit: To skip something is to go by it without notice; the spring feast marking the Exodus has the same name as one word.

clue.text: Sports boat with ski following

parts.note: ff. is the abbreviation for 'and the following' pages

explanation.surface: A small boat for sport, towed with a water-skier behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: ff. in a book reference means 'and the following pages', so it can stand for 'following'.
explanation.definitionFit: A light rowing boat used for racing and sport on rivers.

clue.text: Will Tyndale's version?

definitions.meaning: the document setting out a person's wishes after death
William Tyndale translated the New one of these, the Bible's later half, into English

explanation.definitionFit: A last will is a legal bequest document, and Tyndale's famous translation was of the New one, the Christian scriptures.

clue.text: Sought seed to be planted around garden entrance

indicators.note: the word seed is placed on either side of the other piece, enclosing it like soil

parts.note: an arch is a typical gateway into a garden

explanation.surface: Instructions for sowing seed around the archway into a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planted around' is the container signal: the seed is split and set either side of the arch, with no rearranging needed despite 'to be planted' sounding like one.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean looked for something, the past tense of hunting.

clue.text: Agitated Shire horse?

indicators.note: something agitated is stirred up, so the letters of the breed's name are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A carthorse of the heavy English breed has become nervous and restless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agitated' rearranges SHIRE; a Shire is a heavy English draught breed. The question mark flags a cryptic definition: a horse that shies, starting in fright.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that jumps aside in fright is said to shy, so a nervous horse is one that shies.

clue.text: He knows more on star dispersal

definitions.text: He knows more on star dispersal

indicators.note: scattering these letters about the sky gives them a new order

explanation.surface: A boast about a scientist who knows more about how stars are scattered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispersal' rearranges MOREONSTAR; read as a whole the clue also describes the expert.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who studies stars and other celestial bodies knows more about them than anyone.

clue.text: Boat journey shows evidence passenger vandalism

definitions.meaning: a voyage or excursion by ship
a torn chair cover, a slashed seat, is what a vandal on a bus or train leaves

explanation.surface: A ferry crossing marred by signs that travellers have damaged the fittings.
explanation.walkthrough: Split differently, the letters read as a torn seat, the evidence of vandalism by a passenger.
explanation.definitionFit: A voyage by ship is a journey on the water; read as a damaged seat, it is what a vandal leaves.

clue.text: A drink the teetotal herbalist manages to dig up?

definitions.meaning: a fizzy soft drink flavoured with roots such as sassafras

definitions.text: the teetotal herbalist manages to dig up?
definitions.meaning: a herbalist digs up roots, and that is the only kind of ale a non-drinker can get

explanation.definitionFit: The soft drink flavoured with sassafras is non-alcoholic, and a herb-gatherer digs plant roots from the ground.

clue.text: The daydream of a churchman beside a great lake

indicators.note: one piece sits next to the other in the answer

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a clergyman
Erie is one of North America's Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A clergyman muses dreamily by a vast lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of absorbed musing, being lost in pleasant thoughts.

clue.text: Drive back about four, though it means putting one off

indicators.note: the first word goes round the other, surrounding it

parts.note: to repulse an attacker is to drive them back
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Fighting off an attack by a group of four is described as off-putting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; 'though it means' is only a link to the definition 'putting one off'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disgusting causes revulsion and makes people avoid it.

clue.text: When you do, the telephone will be no longer engaged

definitions.text: When you do, the telephone will be no longer engaged

parts.words: When you do, the telephone will be no longer engaged
parts.note: ending a call by hanging up frees the line, so it no longer gives the busy tone

explanation.definitionFit: Ending a phone call frees the line, which is then no longer in use.

clue.text: Gang leader represents a warning of course to the whole race

parts.note: fore is the warning shouted on a golf course
man can mean mankind, the whole human race

explanation.surface: Someone at a race meeting shouts a caution to all the runners at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' means on a golf course, not 'naturally'.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a work gang or crew of labourers supervises the others.

clue.text: Airborne soldier has favourite place for a suicidal leap

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A paratrooper has a favourite spot for jumping, joked as though from a rooftop.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a parachute jump, but the definition is the low wall on a roof or bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A low protective wall along a roof edge or bridge is where a jumper might stand.

clue.text: Contrition expressed by the last letter from Penzance

indicators.note: the letter is taken away from the town's name

parts.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Remorse is shown in the final letter written from a Cornish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Penzance is a town in Cornwall. 'the last letter' looks like a farewell note, but it is Z, the alphabet's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Acts of atonement show sorrow for wrongdoing, the outward form of remorse.

clue.text: Plutocrat heard turning down Monkhouse's request

indicators.note: the words are spoken, so their sound gives the answer

parts.note: saying no to Bob Monkhouse would be 'Nah, Bob'

explanation.surface: A rich man is overheard refusing what a comedian asked for.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob Monkhouse was a British comedian and game-show host, so refusing him is 'Nah, Bob'.
explanation.definitionFit: A very rich, important man, originally a returned East India Company magnate.

clue.text: What to do when roasting a best cut

indicators.note: the words are chopped up and their letters put in a new order

explanation.surface: Advice on cooking the finest joint of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' looks like a joint of meat, but it signals rearranging ABEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooks spoon fat or juices over meat while it is in the oven.

clue.text: Two things door pranksters do, but there's usually a hitch to it

definitions.text: there's usually a hitch to it

parts.note: children ring a doorbell and then run off
after ringing they bolt, running away

explanation.surface: Kids play the doorbell trick, though there is usually a snag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hitch' means a snag on the surface but is a knot tied to the fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal fitting with a ring through its eye, to which a rope is tied or hitched.

clue.text: The spy who was not keen

definitions.meaning: Anthony ..., the art historian exposed as a Soviet spy
keen here means sharp, as of a blade

explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Blunt was one of the Cambridge spy ring, and a dull edge lacks sharpness.

clue.text: Disfiguring lump can be excised in the pharmacy store

indicators.note: the letters lie inside the run of words

explanation.surface: A lump on the skin can be removed in the chemist's shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A sac or growth under the skin filled with fluid, a swelling.

clue.text: Ready he was for Marryat as both employer and employee

parts.note: a master employs servants
a man is a manservant, the one employed

explanation.surface: A Victorian novelist's hero is both boss and worker.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Marryat's 1841 novel is titled with this name followed by Ready.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Marryat's novel has this as his first name, with Ready as his surname.

clue.text: One Mitford girl

definitions.meaning: oneness, the state of being single and whole
... Mitford, one of the famous Mitford sisters

explanation.definitionFit: Oneness means being undivided; the Mitford sisters were a celebrated English family of six girls, one of whom had this name.

clue.text: Regrets sure to be perturbing

indicators.note: the word sure is disturbed so its letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's regrets are sure to be troubling them.
explanation.definitionFit: To regret something is to feel sorry about it.

clue.text: Having assumed a clerical habit recommended by the stockbroker

definitions.meaning: as two words, wearing a priest's robe: in a vestment
money put into shares, a purchase to make a return

explanation.definitionFit: Split as two words it means dressed in priestly robes; a broker advises putting money into shares for profit.
